BLOCKER on (A) — GitHub refuses private→public issue transfers.

## What happened

Attempted the first transfer (oldest archive issue #3) as the warm-up:
```
$ gh issue transfer 3 jdtogni78/ai-harness --repo jdtogni78/ai-harness-archive
GraphQL: Old issue cannot be transferred from private repository to public repository (transferIssue)
```

This is a GitHub policy, not a permission gap. Source visibility (PRIVATE) > destination visibility (PUBLIC) is blocked outright. Confirmed:
- jdtogni78/ai-harness          : PUBLIC
- jdtogni78/ai-harness-archive  : PRIVATE

So **none** of the 38 issues can be transferred under the current visibility configuration. No work has been done — paused at issue #1 of 38 per your "if you hit a snag, pause and route back" rule.

## Options for the boss

(A1) Temporarily flip jdtogni78/ai-harness-archive to PUBLIC, transfer all 38, flip it back to PRIVATE.
     - Pros: only path that preserves comments + URL redirects + Project-board auto re-point.
     - Cons: brief PUBLIC window on a repo that contains pre-scrub git history — the very reason ai-harness-archive was kept private when the sanitized public ai-harness fork was created. Even a few minutes of PUBLIC exposes the unscrubbed log to GitHub's search-index crawl, which may persist after the flip back. Memory item `project_ai_harness_public_portfolio` records this as the sensitivity that drove the public/archive split.
     - Mitigation: do it during a quiet window; flip back the instant the last transfer lands.

(A2) Flip jdtogni78/ai-harness to PRIVATE temporarily, transfer, flip back to PUBLIC.
     - Pros: doesn't expose archive history.
     - Cons: anyone watching the portfolio repo (or any inbound link) sees a 404 / restricted page during the window; also the portfolio purpose is briefly defeated. Same indexing concern in reverse (cached public state vanishes briefly).

(A3) Recreate each archive issue under jdtogni78/ai-harness via `gh issue create`, copying title + body + labels + state, then close the source with a "moved to #M" comment.
     - Pros: no visibility flip needed; full control over which fields to copy.
     - Cons: loses comments, loses commenter identities, loses old URLs (no redirect — links to archive#N return "not found in your view" for non-collaborators).

(A4) Fall back to Option 2 from the original ticket — document the `--repo jdtogni78/ai-harness-archive` workaround in OPERATIONS + skills helpers. Cheapest, fully reversible. No transfer attempted.

(A5) Hybrid: do (A4) now (cheap), keep the (A1) door open for a later quiet-window batch.

## My read

If the archive's pre-scrub history is genuinely sensitive (memory says it was the basis of the public/archive split), I'd be wary of (A1) without an explicit OK from the boss that a short PUBLIC window on the unscrubbed log is acceptable. (A3) is the next-cleanest in terms of confidentiality but loses comment chains. (A4) gets us the ticket's *secondary* benefit (no skills break on legacy URLs) without the transfer risk.

Even a few seconds of public visibility on the archive would seed GitHub's search index with that material, and the flip-back doesn't unindex it. (A1) trades a permanent risk for a transient board-UI tidy. (A2) defeats the portfolio's whole point during the window. (A3) loses the multi-agent claim-comment history. **(A4) gets the operational win** (skills/helpers no longer trip on the legacy URLs) **without touching visibility**.

If you want a longer-term plan, file a `#XX archive→public migration after history-scrub` ticket once `#13` lands — then (A1) becomes viable because the archive history would also be sanitized.
